payload.rationale: The base rate of US measles cases exceeding 6,000 in a single year since the disease was declared eliminated in 2000 is 0%. The highest recent peak was 1,282 cases in 2019, driven by outbreaks in under-vaccinated communities. Reaching over 6,000 cases would require a catastrophic drop in national vaccination rates and multiple large, sustained outbreaks that overwhelm public health containment efforts. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that the US still maintains high overall MMR vaccination coverage, and aggressive public health interventions usually contain outbreaks well before they reach even a thousand cases. The strongest reason the estimate could be too low is that vaccine hesitancy and anti-vaccine sentiment have grown in recent years, meaning pockets of unvaccinated individuals could theoretically sustain a much larger outbreak than seen in recent decades if introduced by international travelers.
limitations: No current research or case counts for 2026 supplied.
Relies on historical base rates which may not capture recent shifts in vaccine hesitancy.
